candidates: Avoid unexplained numeric literals ('magic numbers') in renderer and layout code. Any raw number whose meaning is not self-evident (e.g., pixel offsets, measurement thresholds, layout constants) must be extracted into a named constant with a descriptive identifier so that its purpose is immediately clear and easy to change consistently.

In Cypress tests, do not wrap assertions in a bare `cy.then(() => { … })` unless there is a genuine asynchronous ordering dependency — specifically, a value computed in a prior `.then()` step that must be captured before assertions can run. Prefer chaining `.should()` or `.and()` directly off the subject command, and keep the style consistent with surrounding tests in the same file.

When implementing text-wrapping logic for diagram labels, ensure the algorithm is fully recursive or iterative so that *every* segment produced after a split is re-checked against the maximum width constraint. A single-pass approach will silently leave over-limit lines whenever input text is pathologically long; the wrapping must keep subdividing (or hyphenating) any segment that still exceeds the limit before it is rendered.
